why: Reproduced by driving state=timeline.owner-flight and pressing .b-grab: #b-edit renders both .b-input fields as bordered boxes (1px solid rgba(17,17,17,.28), radius 6) at exactly the seat's widths — 936px at 1280, 1096px at 1440, 1576px at 1920, computed max-width 'none' — holding 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' (27ch) and '1 August 2026' (13ch), while every other mark in the panel ends by x=495 (steppers 213-425, Shown/Hidden 350-495, Close 213-277, .b-ceiling capped at 46ch). The seat's second charge is wrong, though: the ~88px head band is not an oversight but master.html:7424 `padding-top: 88px` plus the documented round-1 reserve at :7425 ('so filling it cannot move the stepper the owner is about to press again'), and I measured the stepper holding at editor-relative y=247.6 across +7 and -1 presses. Decisive: the exact cap already exists in-house at master.html:8013-8016 but is trapped inside @media (max-width: 1023px), whose own comment names this identical symptom ('a date field holding "25 July 2026" drawn 1221px across').
sharpenedFix: Do NOT collapse the receipt strip — that reverts a paid-for round-1 fix and reintroduces the erasure under the pointer. Instead promote the house's own existing answer out of the @media (max-width: 1023px) block at master.html:8013-8016 and make it the base .b-edit rule: `[data-app="timeline"] .b-edit { justify-items: start; }`, `[data-app="timeline"] .b-edit > * { max-width: 480px; width: 100%; }`, and the companion `[data-app="timeline"] .b-edit .b-seg { justify-self: start; width: auto; }`. .b-edit is already display:grid so justify-items applies; the children keep width:100% so the phone is untouched. Leave `[data-app="timeline"] .b-edit .b-undo { right: auto; width: min(480px, calc(100% - 32px)); max-width: none; }` inside the ≤1023 block — the absolutely-positioned bar is stretched by its own insets and its reserved 88px band must stay.

why: Drove the More tile in notes.notebook, tasks.board and timeline.desk, on pointer and on Enter: every open leaves aria-expanded="true" with .morePop in the DOM while the live region reads "More, closed.", and every close leaves aria-expanded="false" with no .morePop while it reads "More, open." — reversed in both directions, all three products. The cause is confirmed by a control experiment: with reducedMotion:"reduce" the same build announces "More, open." correctly, because morph() at master.html:11311 then calls mutate() synchronously instead of inside document.startViewTransition's async callback, so the say() at :11443 reads the un-flipped moreOpen. Projects (:14990) and Settings both announce truthfully when driven, so More is the only door in the suite lying about its own state.
sharpenedFix: The seat's swap is correct and is the right minimal change — at master.html:11443 replace say(moreOpen ? "More, open." : "More, closed.") with say(wasOpen ? "More, closed." : "More, open."). Prefer wasOpen over moving say() into the callback: wasOpen is captured at :11431 before either branch of morph() runs, so it stays correct on BOTH paths, including the reduced-motion path that is already right today and that a naive relocation could regress. While there, move the plus.focus() at :11441-11442 into the same mutate callback (Projects' shape at :14990) so focus is taken after paintRail() rebuilds rather than before it — it survives today only because paintRail happens to reuse the tile node. Add the interaction-check assertion the seat asks for, but read aria-expanded and the live region in the SAME pass after the transition settles, and run it under both default and reduced motion — a single-motion assertion would have passed this build.

why: Cross-tabulated every font-size/letter-spacing pair in src/notes.css: the ramp is 11/12/13/15/17/20/27/34 and the curve is 34/27/21/18/16/14/12/11, so t-13 borrows tr-14 (19 rules) AND tr-12 (2), t-15 borrows tr-14 (4) AND tr-16 (2), t-17 borrows tr-18 (5), tr-16 (2) AND tr-21 (1) — exactly as the seat said, plus two it missed (.groupBtn pairs t-12 with tr-11, and the expressive .emptyTitle pairs t-27 with tr-34). I drove the seam to the receipt and reproduced the visible instance: .peelSent computes 17px/600/-0.272px directly against .readBody, .pick and .sent at 17px/400/-0.357px — same size, heavier weight, looser fit. Stronger evidence the seat missed: shell.css:686 sets .moreItem { font-size:13px; letter-spacing: var(--tr-13) }, and because no 13 step exists in the Notes curve and .moreItem sits on the ink floor outside both [data-app] scopes, I measured its computed letter-spacing as literally 'normal' — a declared letterfit that silently does nothing on the More menu's own door items.
sharpenedFix: Re-index as the seat proposes, and note the numbers are not inventions: tasks.css already declares --tr-13: -0.010em and --tr-15: -0.016em on [data-app="tasks"], the exact values proposed, so this converges the two labs' curves rather than opening a third. Two corrections. (1) Add the missing shell step, which is the only rendering bug here: .moreItem's var(--tr-13) resolves to nothing on the floor — declare the 13 step on the shell beside the existing `#deck .word { letter-spacing: -0.022em }` (shell.css:543), where the wordmark precedent already puts a cross-product step, or the More menu keeps setting at browser-default tracking after the Notes block is fixed. (2) Do not sweep blindly: [data-app="notes"][data-type="expressive"] .emptyTitle (notes.css:1566) pairs t-27 with tr-34 inside a deliberate expressive-variant block — decide it, don't fold it — and .groupBtn (t-12 + tr-11) needs the same call. Deleting --tr-21/-18/-16/-14 afterwards is safe: shell.css only mentions --tr-18 in a comment and hardcodes the wordmark, and the Tasks curve is separately scoped.

why: Reproduced all of it. Focus [data-act="review"] at 1440 and step the viewport down: it holds at 1400, 1300, 1200, 1199, 1100, 900, 800, 760 and 721, and lands on <body> exactly at 720 — the element still exists and is visible at 390 — and it is still on <body> after widening back to 1440. Same for [data-act="photo"] and the seam's [data-act="send"]; .topField survives because it is a TEXTAREA; Tasks holds focus on all three controls I tried and Timeline lands on its H1, so Notes alone drops it. Nothing announces the loss and the next Tab lands on [data-act="scope"] in the sheet head, not where the person was. Code and gate check out: master.html:19096 gates the capture on TEXTAREA/INPUT, :19135 writes mount.innerHTML, and interaction-check.mjs:1467 asserts layout, lanes, rows, sideways scroll and console noise with no activeElement read.
sharpenedFix: The seat's direction is right and matches the house's own recorded reasoning at master.html:19105 ('the selector alone does not survive a width change'), but data-act alone is too narrow. I verified .idxRow — the index rows, the most-used focusable in Notes and a roving-tabindex list (tabindex values 0 and -1 across 14 rows) — carries data-id but NO data-act, and it drops focus at 720 exactly like the buttons; the seat's fix would leave it dropping. So capture { act: active.dataset.act, id: active.dataset.id, at: active.dataset.i, role: active.getAttribute('aria-label') } and re-find on data-act OR data-id, whichever is present. Two corrections to the seat's re-find: data-act is unique inside [data-app="notes"] at both 1440 and 390 (I counted; no duplicates), so querySelector is safe here — but use aria-label as a tiebreak among candidates, NOT as a veto, or a control whose label legitimately rewords across the breakpoint silently keeps dropping. And after focusing, re-set the roving tabindex=0 onto the restored row, or the index is focused but arrow-walking resumes from the wrong anchor. Finally extend interaction-check.mjs:1467 to read document.activeElement on both sides of the crossing for all three products — the assertion as written could never have caught this.

why: Reproduced every measurement. Diffing all computed properties of .headNext and both children between rest and :hover gives exactly 0 changes on all three, and a rendered 700x60 crop of the head band is byte-identical at 3805 bytes in both states (Buffer.compare === 0). The cause is confirmed in source: master.html:4433 sets .headNext:hover b { color: var(--ink) } while :4186 defines --ink-1: var(--ink), so the hover repaints #111111 as #111111. The control itself is real and good — pressing it takes the index from 14 rows to 3, flips the h1 to 'Your notes, narrowed', sets aria-pressed=true with the indigo inset underline and prints an 'All 14 notes' way-out — and its opposite number [data-act="projects"] in the Tasks head ships a real SVG chevron, which I captured side by side. One correction to the seat: cursor:pointer IS set at rest, so a pointer sweeping the head does get a cursor change; it registered as zero-changed because it is already on, not because it is absent. That is still no rest mark, nothing for touch, and nothing for a scanning eye.
sharpenedFix: Take .projSwitch's whole idiom rather than inventing a new one. (1) Append the same chevron SVG after the date span, but with `flex: none; align-self: center; color: var(--ink-3)` — align-self is required because .headNext is align-items:baseline where .projSwitch is align-items:center, so a copied chevron would hang below the line, and flex:none is required because the span carries text-overflow:ellipsis inside `overflow: clip; overflow-clip-margin: 11px` and would otherwise eat the chevron's space. (2) Do NOT use the seat's `inset 0 -1px 0 var(--ink-4)` hairline: --ink-4 is gate-flagged decorative-only at 1.99:1 and an inset hairline is a third affordance idiom in a head that already has two. Paint the hit area that is already there instead — `[data-app="notes"] .headNext:hover::before { background: var(--wash); border-radius: var(--r-chip); }` — which reuses the existing ::before inset of -11px -9px, matches `.headAct:hover { background: var(--wash) }` two rules below it, and matches .projSwitch's background-color hover. (3) Delete the dead rule; note the seat's line numbers drift — it is master.html:4433 (src/notes.css:290), and --ink-1 is master.html:4186 (src/notes.css:43). (4) Check the chevron at the ≤720 branch, master.html:5772-5778, where .head .headNext goes white-space:normal and the span drops to --t-12; it must not wrap onto a second line there.

why: The seat's measurements are all correct — I drove client+overdue and got lanes reading 0/3, 0/3, 0/2, 0, 0/5, the empty board printing 'No overdue task is on the board for Mara & Finn. All 13 are hidden.', and the head still at '5 of 13 done', fill 38%, aria-valuenow=5 aria-valuemax=13, identical in List view. But this is not an omission: master.html:11826 states the rule in as many words — 'The header counts the whole project. The board shows what is being looked at. Filtering must never change what "5 of 13 done" means' — with :11836 reaffirming it for search and :11797 recording the blocker that produced it ('the board said "5 of 32 done" above a Done column labelled 9'). The seat's fix reverses that decision and is measurably worse: I turned the overdue chip on alone and counted 1 shown, 0 of it done, so recomputing would put '0 of 1 done — 0%' with an empty bar in the head of a project that is 38% done.
sharpenedFix: Keep the denominator. The residual worth fixing is narrow and is the empty-board case only: on a board showing nothing, a filled 38% bar is the loudest mark on screen and is unlabelled about its scope. Two small changes, neither of which touches what '5 of 13 done' means. (1) When filtering() is true, append the scope to the meter's accessible name only — aria-label 'Across the whole project: 5 of 13 done, 38 percent' — and leave the visible sentence, aria-valuemin/max/now and the fill exactly as they are, so the reader gets the qualifier the eye gets from the lane counts. (2) When the filtered set is empty (shown === 0), do not zero the bar and do not rename it 'Nothing shown' — a role=meter reporting zero asserts zero progress, which is a second untruth. Drop the .pace element from the head entirely for that render; the board already carries 'Nothing matches. No overdue task is on the board for Mara & Finn. All 13 are hidden.' plus a 'Show all work' way out, so nothing is lost and the head stops arguing with the board. Restore it the moment anything is shown, on the existing filter-clear repaint.

why: Measured across nine widths. At 320/390/430/600/720 the wordmark sits at x=25 and the first tick at x=40, and headActions' right edge at 295/365/405/575/695 against .lrowMeta's right at 280/350/390/560/680 — exactly 15px inside on both sides at every phone width, matching the seat. At 721 and above the left contract holds to a pixel (word 116 vs tick 117, word 128 vs tick 129). .board.listBoard computes padding 0px 25px 28px at every width, and the head's inset does drop to 16px below 720 (src/tasks.css:2395). I then injected the seat's rule and re-measured: tick-left equals wordmark-left and lrowMeta-right equals headActions-right to 0px at 320, 360, 390, 430, 600 and 720, with document scrollWidth overflow 0, the list scroller's own overflow 0, nothing clipped, and 721+ byte-for-byte untouched. One correction: the seat's desk-band right figures ('728/728', '1153/1153') are approximate — the dated rows land ~7px inside the head actions, not flush, and an undated row's last ink stops 85px short because the grid reserves an empty 74px `when` column.
sharpenedFix: The rule is correct and verified; fix the citations and make its arithmetic explicit. The declaration to re-scope is at src/tasks.css:466-470 (master.html:1625-1629), not line 1633, and the ≤720 block to put the override in is src/tasks.css:573-580 — which already carries `[data-app="tasks"] .lrow { padding: 9px 6px }` — not line 1740. Put it there and name the dependency, because 10px is not a free number: it is the head's 16px phone inset minus the row's own 6px horizontal padding set four lines above it. Write `[data-app="tasks"] .board.listBoard { padding-inline: 10px; } /* 10 + the row's own 6 = the head's 16 */`, or better `calc(16px - 6px)`, or a later change to the row padding silently breaks the column again with no gate to catch it. Also state the hairline consequence the seat left out: .lrow paints the divider as border-bottom 1px rgba(17,17,17,0.06) on the row BOX, so today it runs 34-356 at 390 (9px inside the head column) and after the fix runs 19-371 (6px outside it). That is the desk's own relationship — at 1199 the row box runs 125-1156 against a head column of 128-1153 — so leave the hairline alone; do not inset it to chase the ink.
